proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the true admission lag is longer/variable or if reporting artifacts dominate, a fixed 1-week delayed_I may misalign the peak timing and distort amplitude.
proposals.rationale: Adds an exposed (E) stage to better capture sharp, high-peaked influenza dynamics while mapping hospitalizations to a 1-week lagged infectious proxy, consistent with admissions lagging infection onset.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the true lag is closer to 0–1 weeks, a 2-week delay can shift forecasts late and underfit early growth.
proposals.rationale: Same parsimony as SEIR but allows a longer infection-to-admission delay, which can better align hospitalization-rate peaks when admissions occur after symptom progression.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: H may be weakly identifiable in a short single-season series, leading to parameter tradeoffs (e.g., I→H rate vs. duration in H) and unstable forecasts.
proposals.rationale: Directly models hospitalizations via an explicit H compartment, matching the target semantics (hospitalization rate) and allowing separation between infectious prevalence and admissions.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the observed series is primarily admissions (not a combined burden proxy), I+H can blur interpretation and mis-scale peaks, especially when H is small relative to I.
proposals.rationale: Uses SEIHR but observes a combined burden proxy (I+H) to reduce identifiability pressure on H alone while still allowing hospitalization dynamics to influence the observed signal.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: With only ~31 training weeks, waning-immunity effects may be unidentifiable and can over-flex the trajectory, producing unrealistic rebounds or tail behavior.
proposals.rationale: Allows waning immunity (S↔R) which can accommodate sharper mid-season changes in effective susceptibility while retaining a 1-week admissions lag via delayed_I.
